capabilities: Publish a vault as a static website rendered through Obsidian's own renderer
Publish Bases views as static tables, cards and lists with all rows
Scope which notes publish by folder, excluded folders or a frontmatter flag
Encrypt published pages behind a shared build-time password
Collect reviewer comments on a built site and file them to GitHub, Jira or Asana
extras: Desktop-only (renders through a running Obsidian, Obsidian 1.7.2+); the author flags that scale to large vaults is untested, and that the password lock is a shared secret rather than access control; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Publishers that convert Markdown outside Obsidian cannot reproduce Dataview, Bases and Mermaid output, so those features get skipped or the user is handed a separate static-site generator to configure.

relations.evidence: The plugin commits the built site through the Git Data API and points GitHub Pages at the branch.
Dataview, Datacore, Bases and Mermaid output exists only inside a running Obsidian.
On Obsidian 1.10 or later the plugin does not read the page at all. It registers a view type of its own
An open comment can be filed as an issue in GitHub, Jira or Asana and synced back
An open comment can be filed as an issue in GitHub, Jira or Asana and synced back

summary: Static-site publisher that renders each note through Obsidian's own renderer so Dataview, Bases and Mermaid output survives in the published HTML.
